proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ('Letting u -> 0+ and then epsilon -> 0+ gives Phi(t) >= omega_n for every t in (0, R]'), abstracted from Phi(t) = F(t) t^(-n) mu(B_t(y)) + F(t) - 1 with m(u) = mu(B_u(y)) and alpha = 1 - n/p; the two limits are carried out simultaneously with epsilon = eta.

1. As u -> 0+, Lambda (u/R)^alpha -> 0. Indeed u -> u/R is continuous and vanishes at u = 0, and x -> x^alpha is continuous at x = 0 because alpha > 0, with 0^alpha = 0; hence Lambda (u/R)^alpha -> Lambda * 0 = 0 as u -> 0, in particular as u -> 0+.

2. Fix t with 0 < t <= R and suppose, for a contradiction, that Phi(t) < omega. Put d := omega - Phi(t) > 0 and eta := min{1/2, d/(2(2 omega + 1))}. Then 0 < eta <= 1/2 and eta (2 omega + 1) <= d/2.

3. Each of the following three conditions holds for all sufficiently small u > 0: u < t (because t > 0); Lambda (u/R)^alpha < eta (by step 1, since eta > 0); (1 - eta)(omega u^n) <= m(u) (by (H3) with epsilon = eta > 0). Since the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 is proper, there is u > 0 satisfying all three.

4. Since 0 < u < t <= R, (H1) gives |F(u) - 1| <= Lambda (u/R)^alpha < eta. Hence F(u) > 1 - eta >= 1/2 > 0 and F(u) - 1 > -eta.

5. Since u^n > 0, dividing (1 - eta) omega u^n <= m(u) by u^n gives m(u)/u^n >= (1 - eta) omega, and (1 - eta) omega >= 0. Multiplying the inequalities F(u) >= 1 - eta >= 0 and m(u)/u^n >= (1 - eta) omega >= 0 gives F(u) (m(u)/u^n) >= (1 - eta)^2 omega.

6. Therefore Phi(u) = F(u)(m(u)/u^n) + (F(u) - 1) >= (1 - eta)^2 omega - eta >= (1 - 2 eta) omega - eta = omega - eta (2 omega + 1) >= omega - d/2 > omega - d = Phi(t), using (1 - eta)^2 >= 1 - 2 eta and omega > 0.

7. On the other hand 0 < u <= t <= R, so (H2) gives Phi(u) <= Phi(t), contradicting step 6. Hence Phi(t) >= omega. As t in (0, R] was arbitrary, the claim follows.
key_steps: Assume Phi(t) < omega and set eta = min{1/2, (omega - Phi(t))/(2(2 omega + 1))}.
Choose small u in (0, t) with Lambda (u/R)^alpha < eta and m(u) >= (1 - eta) omega u^n.
Then F(u) >= 1 - eta > 0, so Phi(u) >= (1 - eta)^2 omega - eta > Phi(t).
This contradicts the monotonicity Phi(u) <= Phi(t).
